s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin lesions with hyperkeratotic plaques and scales
salient_findings: Hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales
key_facts: Lesions did not improve with topical corticosteroids
Symmetrical distribution over dorsum of feet and around knees
Negative hepatitis C and B serologies
Plasma zinc at lower end of normal
Biopsy showed hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin lesions with hyperkeratotic plaques and scales
salient_findings: Hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales
key_facts: Lesions did not improve with topical corticosteroids
Symmetrical distribution over dorsum of feet and around knees
Negative hepatitis C and B serologies
Plasma zinc at lower end of normal
Biopsy showed hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate

differentials: Keratosis linearis with ichthyosis congenita and sclerosing keratoderma
per_call: Keratosis linearis with ichthyosis congenita and sclerosing keratoderma

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic plaques, thick adherent scales, and symmetrical distribution are characteristic of psoriasis

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic plaques, erythema, and presence of thick adherent scales are consistent with pityriasis rubra pilaris

shortlist.label: Lichen simplex chronicus
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic plaques, hyperkeratosis, and perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate are features of lichen simplex chronicus

shortlist.label: Hyperthyroidism-associated dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone and presence of hyperkeratotic plaques suggest a possible link to hyperthyroidism

shortlist.label: Zinc deficiency dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Plasma zinc at lower end of normal and presence of hyperkeratotic plaques raise the possibility of zinc deficiency dermatitis

raw.rationale: The presence of well-defined hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales and a peripheral rim of erythema, along with the biopsy findings of hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate, are characteristic of psoriasis. The symmetrical distribution of lesions over the dorsum of feet and around knees also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic palmoplantar keratoderma and orange-red scaling

rejected.label: Lichen simplex chronicus
rejected.why: Lesions are typically more localized and lack the characteristic symmetrical distribution

rejected.label: Hyperthyroidism-associated dermatitis
rejected.why: While elevated TSH suggests thyroid dysfunction, the skin findings are not typical for hyperthyroidism-associated dermatitis

rejected.label: Zinc deficiency dermatitis
rejected.why: Plasma zinc is at the lower end of normal but not definitively low, and skin findings do not match the typical acral and periorificial distribution
